data.turoyo: Bəṯr məd mdaranne kəmrawšənne bu rawšo, kəmminale zəwoqo
data.translation: Wenn sie das Getreide geworfelt haben, schaufeln sie es mit der Schaufel auf einen Haufen – das nennt man zĭwoqo

rationale: Second Infinitiv example; the named operation in another agricultural account, without changing its uncertain referent boundary.

summary: All four occurrences checked. JL 13.12/11 and /12 are already the two inherited quotations; no repeats. The technical sense and detailed inherited note are preserved.

JTM 1.1/19 names zəwoqo between winnowing/shovel work and coarse sieving. JL describes gradual release through moving air after sieving. This may reflect procedural/dialect differences; it does not independently establish a generic shovelling sense.

Exact and related form lookups mzawqənne/mzawqi, entry zwq and the phrase search found no independent attestation settling the new Preterit claim. məd temporal framing and a completed translation cannot decide the paradigm. The operation name is published in the existing Infinitiv box; no uncertain new finite box is added.
Does zəwoqo in JTM 1.1/19 name shovelling into a pile, a separate fine-cleaning pass, or a regional version of the wind-cleaning operation?
Verify mzawqənne: what are the actor and patient suffixes, and is it Preterit or a bare Infectum in a procedural temporal clause? The reader’s Preterit analysis is not accepted as established.
What explains the different placement of coarse sieving relative to zəwoqo in JL and JTM: technique, dialect or narrative ordering?
